title: Omarchy Mobile is written, and the phone is restarting
body: Every image was written, and the phone confirmed each one: boot_b, init_boot_b, vendor_boot_b, vendor_kernel_boot_b, dtbo_b, userdata.
Slot B is the active slot, and the phone was told to restart. It now starts Omarchy Mobile from slot B. At its first start the system grows to fill the phone's storage, which can take a few minutes.

This version of the installer cannot put your answers on the phone: it has no way yet to write them into the system image. So the phone starts Omarchy Mobile with no user account, no PIN or password and no Wi-Fi set up, and there is nothing to unlock it with. An install made with this version shows that the install itself works; it does not give you a phone you can use.
The radio backup and Google's files for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, sound, camera and modem are not on the phone either: this version of the installer does nothing after the restart.
footer: Android is still on slot A, unused. Its data was erased with userdata, so it needs a factory reset if it is ever started again.
The install guide's "Going back to Android" has the steps to put the phone back as it was sold.
